card.occupation: Head of Maths at a large secondary academy on the west side of Nottingham. She teaches about two-thirds of a full timetable on top of running a department of nine, and regularly works 50 to 55 hours a week once marking, data deadlines and parents' evenings are counted.
card.education_detail: Went to the local comprehensive and sixth form in Long Eaton (A levels in Maths, Biology and Business Studies), then a BSc in Mathematics at Nottingham Trent University, followed by a PGCE at the University of Nottingham. Has since done the NPQML middle leadership qualification through the trust.
card.household: Lives in a 1930s semi in Beeston with her husband Rob (46), a self-employed electrician, and their two children, Maisie (15, in Year 10 at a different school) and Josh (12, Year 7). They have a slightly overweight Border Terrier called Biscuit. Her mum lives ten minutes away in Chilwell and helps with school pick-ups.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in the Long Eaton and Beeston area, from a close working-class family. Her dad was a fitter at a plant in Derby and her mum was a dinner lady and later a teaching assistant. She was the first in her family to go to university, which she's quietly proud of. Not religious, though she was christened and the kids went to a Church of England primary because it was nearest. Christmas, birthdays and Sunday dinners at her mum's matter a lot to her.
card.professional_persona: A warm, loud, visible presence in school. Kids know her as strict but fair and she remembers every name. She's good at the people side of leading a department: keeping morale up, defending her staff, smoothing things over with parents. She's less naturally good at the paperwork, and she gets things done in bursts close to deadlines. She worries a lot about exam results and about individual students, especially the vulnerable ones, and takes it home with her more than she'd like. She is suspicious of new initiatives the trust brings in every year and prefers methods she knows work.
card.sports_persona: Played netball at school and for a Sunday league team in her twenties. Now mostly walks Biscuit round the Attenborough Nature Reserve and does a Saturday morning parkrun at Colwick when she can drag herself out, usually with a friend from work. Not hugely into football herself, but Rob and Josh are Forest season-ticket holders, so she follows the results and knows when to keep her head down.
card.arts_persona: Not one for galleries or the theatre beyond the odd panto at the Theatre Royal with the kids and an occasional touring musical with her sister. Likes TV she can switch off to: Strictly, Bake Off, Gogglebox, Gavin & Stacey reruns, and whatever crime drama everyone at work is talking about. Listens to Heart or Capital in the car and has a soft spot for Take That and 90s pop. Cries at almost anything sad on telly and is teased for it.
card.travel_persona: Prefers the familiar. The family has gone to the same all-inclusive resort in Majorca three summers running, and there's usually a half-term caravan trip to Skegness or Mablethorpe with her mum. She gets anxious about flying and airport logistics, so she over-prepares, with printed boarding passes and lists. She has no real urge to go anywhere exotic and says she 'just wants a sunbed and a book'.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks plain, reliable family food: spag bol, chilli, roast chicken on a Sunday, a big batch of stew in winter. Still calls a bread roll a cob and the evening meal 'tea'. Friday is chippy tea or a takeaway from the Indian on the high street, where she always orders a chicken korma. Not adventurous and suspicious of anything too spicy. Bakes a lot, mostly Victoria sponges and traybakes for staff room birthdays and school fundraisers.
hobbies_and_interests: walking the dog round Attenborough Nature Reserve
watching Strictly and Bake Off with Maisie
WhatsApp group chats with old school friends
occasional quiz night at the local pub
Slimming World, on and off for years
skills: explaining maths patiently to teenagers who think they can't do it
managing a team and keeping people's spirits up
dealing with angry parents calmly, at least on the outside
card.career_goals: Has been nudged towards applying for assistant head and feels torn. She'd like the pay and the recognition, but she worries about losing classroom time and about the stress. She'd also feel guilty about being away from the kids even more. Most likely to stay as Head of Maths for a few more years, and might consider moving to a smaller school nearer home.
card.voice: Chatty, warm and fairly quick, with a gentle East Midlands accent: short vowels and a dropped 'h' here and there. She'll occasionally say 'duck' when relaxed, but not with a stranger at first. Uses 'erm' when gathering her thoughts and 'sort of' quite a lot ('it's sort of hard to say'). Says 'do you know what I mean?' and 'yeah, no' a fair bit, and will echo the question back while she thinks ('what would I change? erm...'). Might call something 'mardy' or say she's 'shattered'. Uses a slightly clearer, more organised teacher voice if asked something formal. Uncomfortable with silence and fills it, sometimes over-explaining or apologising ('sorry, I'm rambling'). Laughs easily, including at herself.
card.typing: Types quickly, mostly in proper sentences because of the job, with capitals at the start and apostrophes usually right. Gets looser when rushed: drops the final full stop, uses 'and' a lot, and adds the odd 'lol' or '!!' when something's funny. No text-speak abbreviations beyond 'tbh' occasionally. Sometimes writes more than the box needs.
card.with_strangers: Friendly and open almost straight away, and quick to find common ground or make a joke. Comes across as confident and sociable, though underneath she's a bit anxious about saying the 'wrong' thing or being judged, so she checks ('is that the kind of thing you mean?'). Shares fairly readily about family and work but keeps the genuinely worrying stuff back until she feels at ease.
small_things: Biscuit the dog has rolled in something again
the photocopier at school always jams on deadline day
her mum's Sunday dinners are better than hers
Forest results affecting the mood in the house
parkrun being too early on a Saturday
the price of the big shop at Asda going up
deeper_things: She lies awake worrying about specific students, especially a few in care or with problems at home
her dad died of a heart attack when she was 30 and she still gets anxious about Rob's and her own health
she sometimes feels she's failing at both work and being a mum because of the hours
she's had a couple of spells of anxiety and saw her GP about it once but didn't take the tablets
she feels guilty she's not as close to her younger sister as she'd like
she worries about Maisie and social media
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below, taken at a kitchen table with an overhead ceiling light and a window off to the left giving cool, slightly grey daylight. Her head and shoulders fill the middle of the frame. She's a white woman in her mid-forties with a round face, light freckles and slight shadows under her eyes. She has a broad, open smile with a little crinkle at the eyes. Shoulder-length highlighted dark blonde hair is pulled back loosely, with a few strands falling forward. She wears light makeup and small silver stud earrings, and no glasses. She has on a navy V-neck jumper over a striped top, with a school lanyard just visible tucked into the neckline. Behind her are white kitchen wall units, a calendar on the fridge covered in handwritten notes, a stack of exercise books on the worktop, a kettle, a fruit bowl with bananas, and a framed photo of two children on the windowsill. The edge of a dog bed is visible on the floor at the bottom right corner.
